 Mahanadi Coalfields IPO Explained on 12 November 2026: SEBI Clears Coal India's 10% Offer for Sale Worth Up to $1 Billion, Launch Possible in Late November or Early December
 Mahanadi IPO: OFS of 66.18 crore shares, 10%. SEBI nod 4 Nov. Up to $1 bn raise. Coal India Rs 404.60 (12 Nov, 3:24 PM). Dates, price band awaited.
 Updated: 12 Nov 2026 • 3:57 pm
 Posted by: Lakshit Sharma 
 Quick Answer 
 The Mahanadi IPO is a pure offer for sale of up to 66.18 crore shares, about 10% of the company, by parent Coal India, and SEBI issued its observations on 4 November 2026. Reports say it could raise up to $1 billion at a valuation of up to $10 billion and open in the second half of November or early December, but the price band, lot size and dates are not announced. Mahanadi earned net profit of Rs 10,698 crore on revenue of Rs 30,550 crore in FY26 with almost no debt, although both have slipped for two years. Because the proceeds go to Coal India, the sale adds no fresh capital to Mahanadi.
 Mahanadi Coalfields IPO moved a step closer after SEBI issued its observations on the draft papers on 4 November 2026, clearing Coal India's subsidiary to launch an offer for sale of up to 66.18 crore shares. Coal India stock traded at Rs 404.60 at 3:24 PM on 12 November 2026, down 0.42%.
 Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL) is India's largest coal producer by volume, and the offer would follow the NSE issue of Rs 22,562 crore in September and the Jio Platforms issue of about Rs 30,188 crore in October. Below is what the MCL IPO offers, how the company has performed, what valuation the market is talking about, how earlier Coal India subsidiary IPOs fared and what the draft prospectus flags as risks.

 Key Details of the MCL IPO 
 Coal India said in March that it could sell up to 25% in subsidiaries Mahanadi Coalfields and South Eastern Coalfields. The draft papers filed on 31 August 2026 show a first sale of 10% in MCL, which is entirely an offer for sale with no fresh issue.

 Mahanadi Coalfields IPO Date and Price Band: What Is Known 
 Nothing official is out yet for the MCL IPO. A Bloomberg report on 2 November said Coal India is preparing to launch the issue as early as this month, and also said that issue size, valuation and launch date may change. The price band, minimum lot and anchor investor date will appear in the red herring prospectus.
 About Mahanadi Coalfields 
 MCL operates mainly in the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields in Odisha and ran 17 mines, 14 opencast and 3 underground, as of 30 June 2026. It produced 218.31 million tonnes in FY26, about 21% of India's domestic coal output and about 28.4% of Coal India's production.
 Audited reserves are 9,840.31 million tonnes, which the DRHP says can support about 45 years of production at the FY26 rate. Opencast mines gave 99.85% of production, and fuel supply agreements, mostly with power utilities, accounted for 82.12% of product-sale revenue.

 FY26 revenue fell about 2.6% and net profit about 1.2%. In the June 2026 quarter revenue rose about 6.4% to Rs 8,033.77 crore, but net profit slipped about 2.0% to roughly Rs 2,398 crore.
 The slide has three causes in the DRHP data. Fuel supply agreements, which follow Coal India's notified prices, rose from 77.46% to 82.12% of product-sale revenue, mining and contract expenditure climbed from about Rs 5,862 crore to Rs 6,824 crore, and FY26 output dropped about 3%. Other income nearly doubled to about Rs 3,350 crore and cushioned reported profit.
 The balance sheet is clean, with borrowings of about Rs 3 crore at March 2026. MCL paid about Rs 7,650 crore in dividends to Coal India in FY26, though that does not guarantee future payouts.
 Mahanadi Coalfields IPO Valuation: What the Numbers Imply 
 The reported $10 billion value is about Rs 90,000 crore at Rs 90 per dollar. On FY26 net profit of Rs 10,698.12 crore and 661.84 crore shares, the table shows illustrative scenarios for the Mahanadi IPO. These are not an announced price band.

 A 10% sale at Rs 90,000 crore is about Rs 9,000 crore. The 8.4x multiple sits above the 7.46x of Coal India but below the industry PE of 9.27 for the parent's sector, so investors in the MCL IPO will weigh the company's lower profit trend against its scale and zero debt.

 Coal India stock gained about 4% when the draft papers for the Mahanadi IPO were filed, and the proceeds of about Rs 9,000 crore, if the issue is priced at the reported value, equal roughly 3.6% of its Rs 2,49,591 crore market capitalisation. Since Coal India keeps about 90% of MCL, only the 10% minority share of MCL profit, roughly Rs 1,070 crore on FY26 numbers or about 3.4% of Coal India's FY26 consolidated profit, would leave its earnings.
 On the chart, Coal India stock is just above its 20-day average of Rs 402.68 and sits 17.6% below its 52-week high of Rs 491.25. The SuperTrend indicator still points down with resistance at Rs 420.05 and support at Rs 377.25. These are reference levels, not recommendations.

 Key Risks in the MCL IPO Draft Prospectus 
 Earnings momentum is the first risk for the MCL IPO, since profit has fallen two years in a row. Customer concentration is the second: thermal power made up 68.62% of FY26 product sales and the top ten customers gave 55.94% of revenue. Top ten contractors accounted for about 60.02% of contractual expenses, and trade receivables rose from about Rs 3,744 crore in March 2026 to Rs 4,220 crore in June 2026.
 Legal exposure is the third. A CAG observation on state mineral levies carries potential exposure of about Rs 31,227.80 crore, which is not a confirmed payable, and the DRHP lists 47 criminal, 105 tax and 52 regulatory proceedings with an aggregate amount of Rs 9,084.80 crore. Longer term, renewable energy growth and power-sector policy could reduce coal demand.
 Should You Apply for the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO? 
 The case for applying to the MCL IPO rests on scale, long reserve life, almost no debt and a profit base above Rs 10,000 crore. The case for waiting rests on falling earnings, concentrated customers and the fact that the offer price is unknown. Many investors wait for the price band and the red herring prospectus before bidding in the Mahanadi IPO, and check the grey market only as an unofficial signal.

 Conclusion 
 The MCL IPO has regulatory clearance, a 10% offer for sale and a reported size of up to $1 billion, but dates, price band and lot size are still to come. MCL offers Rs 10,698 crore of profit and almost no debt, while revenue and profit have slipped for two years and the final price will decide how attractive the entry is.

 Frequently Asked Questions 
 What is the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO? 
 Ans. It is a proposed public issue of up to 66,18,36,300 equity shares of face value Rs 2, about 10% of Mahanadi Coalfields, sold by its parent Coal India. It is entirely an offer for sale, so Mahanadi Coalfields receives no money and the proceeds go to Coal India. The shares are proposed to list on the BSE and NSE, and Coal India would keep about 90% after the sale.
 Has SEBI approved the MCL IPO? 
 Ans. SEBI issued its observations on the draft red herring prospectus on 4 November 2026, which is the regulator's go-ahead to launch the issue. Reports say Coal India could open the IPO in the second half of November or early December 2026, but the company has not confirmed a schedule and the final timing can change.
 How big is the MCL IPO and what valuation is expected? 
 Ans. Reports citing Bloomberg say the IPO could raise as much as $1 billion and value Mahanadi Coalfields at up to $10 billion, which is roughly Rs 90,000 crore at Rs 90 per dollar. Those are reported estimates, and discussions on size, valuation and timing were still ongoing, so the final numbers will be known only when the price band is announced.
 What are the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO date, price band and lot size? 
 Ans. The IPO date, price band, lot size, anchor date and listing date have not been announced as of 12 November 2026. These details are fixed in the red herring prospectus closer to launch. Any grey market premium quoted online is unofficial and should not be treated as a price signal.
 What are the Mahanadi Coalfields financials? 
 Ans. Mahanadi Coalfields reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 30,549.59 crore, down about 2.6%, and net profit of Rs 10,698.12 crore, down about 1.2%, on production of 218.31 million tonnes. In the June 2026 quarter revenue rose about 6.4% to Rs 8,033.77 crore while net profit fell about 2.0% to roughly Rs 2,398 crore. Borrowings were only about Rs 3 crore at March 2026.
 How will the MCL IPO affect Coal India shares? 
 Ans. Coal India gets the sale proceeds and keeps about 90% of Mahanadi, so its consolidated earnings change only by the roughly 10% minority share of Mahanadi profit, which is about 3.4% of Coal India's FY26 consolidated profit on a simple calculation. Coal India shares rose about 4% when the draft papers were filed, and the stock trades at Rs 404.60 with a PE of 7.46 and a dividend yield of 6.54%.
 What are the key risks of the MCL IPO? 
 Ans. The main risks are two years of falling revenue and profit, dependence on thermal power customers at 68.62% of product sales, top ten customers at 55.94% of revenue, rising receivables, a CAG observation on state mineral levies with potential exposure of about Rs 31,227.80 crore that is not a confirmed payable, and continued control by Coal India. The price band will decide how much of this is already priced in.
 Should I apply for the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO? 
 Ans. Wait for the price band and the red herring prospectus before deciding, because the offer price decides the valuation. At the reported Rs 90,000 crore value, the IPO would price Mahanadi at about 8.4 times FY26 profit, against a PE of 7.46 for parent Coal India. Earlier Coal India subsidiary IPOs had mixed outcomes, with Bharat Coking Coal subscribed 143.85 times and CMPDI listing at a discount.
